title: From Outcomes to Actions: Leveraging Hindsight for Long-Horizon Language Agent Training
claim: Existing RL methods fail on long horizons: critic-free training collapses as interactions lengthen, while critic-based training stays stable but learns slowly.
layout: single line plot, training steps on x-axis, legend on top, collapse curve highlighted
description: A single line chart of training reward (y-axis, 0 to 0.8) against training step (x-axis, 0 to 400). A legend across the top lists three runs: GRPO with 4 turns (blue), GRPO with 2 turns (orange) and PPO with 4 turns (green). The blue curve climbs fastest and peaks near 0.78 around step 150–190. It then drops sharply and falls to zero by about step 320, which shows collapse. The orange curve plateaus around 0.65–0.68. The green curve starts slowly, with a long warmup plateau near 0.22 for about 40 steps. It then rises steadily and reaches about 0.8 by step 300. Light gray gridlines, bold serif labels. The eye goes first to the blue collapse.
caption: Existing RL methods struggle in long-horizon interactions. GRPO becomes unstable with longer-horizon interactions, while PPO remains stable but converges slowly due to critic warmup.
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become a widely adopted technique for improving large language models (LLMs) on complex tasks. Despite this progress, existing RL methods still face challenges in training agents with longer-horizon interactions. One major bottleneck is distinguishing the contribution of different actions in long-horizon interaction, leading to high optimization variance. To address this, we introduce a novel policy gradient method, Hindsight Policy Optimization (HPO), that projects both the current policy distribution and the hindsight distribution into an intent space and extracts low-variance learning signals from the Wasserstein distance between them. We theoretically and empirically show that aggregating semantically similar states and actions in the intent space yields a bounded-variance estimator and improves policy performance stably. Our code is available online.
